Sabang Settlers Association Baybay, Leyte Dear Punong Barangay Urbona: This has reference to your letter-query seeking the legal opinion of this Department concerning the rules on Vacancies and Succession as provided in the Local Government Code of 1991 particularly in Sections 44 and 45 of the said Code. In this regard, we would like to inform you that this Department had already answered a similar query in DILG Opinion No. 25, series ot 2008 that permanent vacancies in the sangguniang barangay where automatic successions do not apply shall be filled by appointment by the City or Municipal Mayor, upon recommendation ot the sangguniang barangay concerned [Sec. 45 (a) (3) Local Government Code]. Attached herewith is a copy of the said DILG opinion tor your ready reference. Very truly yours, By Authority of the Secretary: JESU . DOQUVIV Director III

WAGIAPON Barangay 4, Hinigiran Negros Occidental Dear Mr. Lagtapon: This has reference to your earlier letter asking our legal opinion on whether or not succession as provided under the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160) is applicable in case the elected Punong Barangay died before taking his oath and assume the functions of his office. At the outset, please be informed that the rule on succession is embodied under Sections 44 and 46 of the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160) pertaining to the manner of filling-up of permanent vacancies in the Offices of the Governor, Vice-Governor, Mayor and Vice-Mayor and on temporary vacancy in the office of the local chief executive, respectively, and not Section 64 as erroneously stated in your letter. Nevertheless, in reply to your query, we answer in the affirmative. Allow us to illustrate how we arrived to this conclusion. Well-settled is the rule that a person acquires public office either by appointment or by election. An appointment is the act or designation-by the executive officer, board or body to where that power has been delegated, of the individual who is to exercise the functions of a given office (Mechem, Section 102). On the other hand, an election "means [he choice or selection of candidates to public office by popular vote through the use electorate. An ('Icc/ ion is the embodiment of IIIC popular iVill, thc expression OJ' the sovereign pcnver of the people. Thc zoinner is the candidate who has obtained a majority or plurality of valid votes cast in IIIC election" (Rulloda vs. COMELEC, G.R. No. 154198, January 20, 2003). As you represented, the Punong Barangay was duly elected as such. His election to said position would therefore mean that he acquired a plurality of the votes lavvfully cast in his barangay. "The fact of having a (Mechem, note 2 at 130, cited in De Leon, H. Jr. Law on Public Offices and Election Law, 1990 Edition, p. 374).

Subsequent to one's election to office and before entering upon the performance of his duties, the person so elected is usually required by law to do some acts by which he shall signify his acceptance of the office and his undertaking to execute the trust confided in him. Section 92 of the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160) provides and we quote: . — (a) All elective and appointive local "SECTION 92. oath officials employees shall, upon assumption to office, subscribe to an oath or affirmation Of office in [he prescribed forni. xxx" Such act wherein the person elected shall signify his acceptance of the office and his undertaking to execute the trust confided in him is It generally consists of the taking, and ordinarily termed qualification. often of subscribing and filing of an official oath. Accordingly, failure to take an oath and assume the powers, duties and functions of the office would result to a failure to qualify, which, in turn, is one of the grounds enumerated under Section 44 of the Local Government Code that would render an office permanently vacant. Said provision provides and we quote: "Section 44. Permanent Vacancies in the Offices of [Ite Governor, Vice-Governor, Mayor, and Vice-Mayor.— xxx xxx xxx If a perrnanent vacancy occurs in [he office o/' the (b) punong bitrangilll, the highest ranking sangguniang bara.nga!/ mentber or, in case o/' his pernmnent inability, the second highest ranking sanggunian member, shall bcconw the punong barangay. xxx xxx xxx (d) The successors as defined herein shall serve only the nncxpired tcrrns of their predecessors. For purposes of this Chapter, a permanent vacancy arises when an elcvtive local official fills a higher vacant office, refuses to diest is removed front office, assume ctffice, fails to qualily, voluntarily resigns, or is othercvisc permanently incapacitated to discharge I he functions of his office. For purposes of succession as provided in this Chapter, ranking in Ille sanggunian shall be determined on the basis of the proportion o/' votes obtained each winning candidate [o the the innnediatel!/ preceding local election." (Emphasis Supplied) Applying the foregoing to your case, by reason of his death, the elected Punong Barangay can no longer assume and take his oath of office. His failure to assume and take his oath of office will, as mentioned above, result to his failure to qualify to the office of the Punong Barangay. Since there is failure to qualify on his part, this would thereafter render his position permanently vacant and there being a permanent vacancy in the office of the Punong Barangay, the rule on succession as provided under the aforequoted Section 44 (b), supra, is therefore applicable. Based on the aforequoted provision, in case of permanent vacancy in the office of the

Punong Barangay, the highest-ranking sangguniang barangay member or, in case of his permanent inability, the second highest-ranking sangguniang barangay member shall become the Punong Barangay. Hence, after the highest ranking sangguniang barangay member could have taken his oath of office as such and assumed the functions, powers and duties thereof, he can now succeed, by operation of law, the permanently vacant office of the Punong Barangay by simply applying the aforequoted rule of succession. It is, however, required . that he shall likewise take anew an oath of office, this time as Punong Barangay. Subsequent vacancies in the sangguniang barangay shall be filled automatically by other sanggunian members according to their ranking. Such being the case, there will be a resultant vacancy, specifically the seventh ranking member in the sangguniang barangay after applying the rule of succession. The seventh place vacancy in the sangguniang sangguniang barangay shall be filled up by appointment to be issued by the municipal mayor pursuant to Section 45 (a) and O of the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160) which provide and we quote: "SECTION 45. Permanent Vacancies in the Sanggunimt. — (a) Permanent vacancies in the sanggunian coltere automatic successions provided above do not apply shall be filled btf appointment in [Ile following ntanner: (1) xxx xxx xxx (2) xxx xxx xxx (3) The city or municipal mayor, in the case of sangguniang barangay, upon recommendation of the sangguniang I;nrangay concerned. xxx xxx xxx O In case the permanent vacancy is caused by a sanggunian member does not belong to any political party, thc local chief upon recommendation of thc sanggunian executive shall, concerned, appoint a qualified person to fill the vacancy. ' xxx xxx xxx Nowhere can we find in pertinent laws or even in jurisprudence that in case of permanent vacancy in the office of the punong barangay under the same circumstance, the second placer in the election shall become the punong barangay. In fact, in many jurisprudence decided by the Supreme Court, said Court maintained on the contrary, that is, the non-proclamation of the second placer simply means he lost in the election. The ratiocination given by the Supreme Court in the case of Reyes vs. COMELEC (254 SCRA 514), is quite enlightening and we quote: "That the candidate who obtains the second highest Titnnber of -ootes may •not be proclaimed winner in case the winning candidate is disqualified is nozv settled.
